# cancho-gpu

> lex-gpu's .chx tile-kernel compiler, written in cancho: it checks a typed tile program (linearity, bounds, shapes, the threadgroup budget) and lowers it to CUDA C and Metal, byte-identical with lex-gpu's Rust emitter on 159 cases (133 emit, 26 refused by both). It links only libc; its authority report names what it may do (args, stderr, file read and write, heap, stdout) and no network or foreign code. Alpha: the compiler, device path, model-reading core (GGUF, safetensors, BPE tokenizer, sampler) and the decode kernels of an attention layer are built; a model runner runs Qwen2.5-0.5B on a Metal GPU and agrees with Hugging Face transformers (same greedy tokens, top-5 logits within 1e-4).

## Use it
- [Quick start](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu#quick-start): build the compiler at the pinned revision, emit a kernel.
- Commands: `cancho-gpu emit <file.chx> <dir> [name=value ...] [--run]`, `cancho-gpu check <file.chx> [name=value ...] [--run]`, `cancho-gpu gguf <file.gguf> [--sum]`, `cancho-gpu safetensors <file>`, `cancho-gpu tokenize <tokenizer.json|model.gguf> <corpus>`, `cancho-gpu sample <logits.f32> <vocab> <temperature> <top_p> <top_k> <seed>`. A refusal is `error[<rule>]: <message>` on stderr, exit 1; a usage mistake is exit 2.

## Facts that matter when calling it
- Targets: nvidia-ada (CUDA C) and apple-m-series (Metal), each from the file's schedule. amd-cdna3 is a schedule row with no emitter.
- Device paths: Metal has run on Apple Silicon (reach and numerical agreement, not speed). CUDA is verified against a mock driver only; no real NVIDIA GPU run yet.
- `gguf` reads the first 32 MiB of a file: metadata and tensor directory, never tensor values. It refuses hostile input with a rule tag (gguf-truncated, gguf-version, gguf-duplicate, ...).
- Kernels: rope, kv_append, attention (head dimension 256; at most 1364 positions on Metal) and attn_gate in tests/chx/. Split-KV attention for longer contexts cannot be written in the surface yet.
- Model runner: `cancho-gpu-run <model dir> tests/chx "<prompt>" <new tokens>` for Qwen2-architecture bf16 checkpoints (256-position context, no chat template), 6 to 12 ms a token. Qwen3.8-27B: `cancho-gpu-run35 <ollama store> tests/chx "<prompt>" <new tokens>` runs `qwen3.8:27b-mlx` (NVFP4, 48 gated-delta layers) at about 24 tokens a second, matching a reference's golden log-probabilities to 1e-4 (256-position context).
- Not implemented: serving, quantised weights, linear attention, AMD, Hopper.

- [Design](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/design.md): how the compiler is built and every difference from the Rust.
- [Device](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/device.md): driving a GPU, and what stays unproven.
- [Runtime](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/runtime.md): the GGUF and safetensors readers, the tokenizer and the sampler.
- [Inference](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/inference.md): running Qwen2.5-0.5B on a Metal GPU.
- [Qwen3.8-27B](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-gpu/blob/main/docs/qwen35.md): the 27B runner, its kernels and how it is checked.
